title: Existence of strict scalar association on fixed quotient representatives
statement: Fix a prime l, finite coefficient fields E,L over Q_l, a coefficient homomorphism iota:E→L, a scheme W, the derived coefficient calculi SE,SL, scalar systems A for E→L and A0 for the identity on E, and reduction-model data d,d0 [stage3-pur-extension-reduction-data]. For every good integral cochain complex K there is an isomorphism of whole strict sequence-site complexes S_iota(d0.direct K) ≅ d.direct K [def-trf-integral-comparison-sequence-systems]. On every degree i, level n, pro-etale object U and local tensor b tensor (a tensor x), it sends the inverse-evaluation representative to the inverse-evaluation representative of iota(a)*b tensor x. Sections are transported from finite evaluation by integralComparisonSequenceSection [def-trf-integral-comparison-realization-models]. This is existence of the normalized association only; it does not assert uniqueness, existence of d or d0, or any geometric or completed comparison.

source.place: Compatibility with coefficient extension; Tags 03EL and 07A4; quotient association in proof steps 1--2 of lem-pur-scalar-extension-tower-coherence.

proof.text: Use scalar cochain evaluation to identify evaluation of sequence-site scalar extension with finite scalar extension. Conjugate by the two directEvaluation isomorphisms. Compose the extension/restriction adjunctions to obtain finite balanced tensor association, sending b tensor (a tensor x) to iota(a)*b tensor x; the inverse inserts one. The unit normalization fixes its action on the actual sections in the statement. These maps are cochain maps by naturality.

The direct_transition equations identify the two successor maps with reduction of coefficients. Since ring maps preserve multiplication and one, finite association and its inverse commute with successor transitions. Compose successor squares to cover all quotient maps. Assemble the degreewise module isomorphisms on the product sequence site using systemIsoOfEvaluation_exists. Ordinary evaluation is jointly faithful, so cochain compatibility gives a strict complex isomorphism with the displayed section formula. This constructs the association; it makes no assertion about uniqueness, geometric pullback, completed scalar comparisons or derived limits. The same formulas include n=0 and zero complexes and use no flatness of the quotient inclusion.

proof_origin.place: D3: isolate the strict association construction; model existence, uniqueness by generators, and the geometric square are assembled in quotientModels.

theorem quotientAssociation_exists
    (W : Scheme.{u})
    (SE : CoefficientDerivedSystemCalculus.{u, u} l E W)
    (SL : CoefficientDerivedSystemCalculus.{u, u} l L W)
    (A : CoefficientExtensionSystems.{u, u} l E L ι W)
    (A0 : CoefficientExtensionSystems.{u, u} l E E (AlgHom.id ℚ_[l] E) W)
    (d : CoefficientExtensionReductionData.{u, u} l E L ι W SE SL A)
    (d0 : CoefficientExtensionReductionData.{u, u} l E E (AlgHom.id ℚ_[l] E) W SE SE A0)
    (K : (integralOperationsGoodComplex.{u, u} l E W).FullSubcategory) :
    ∃ δ : (scalar l E L ι W).obj (d0.direct.obj K) ≅ d.direct.obj K,
      ∀ (n : ℕ) (i : ℤ) (U : W.ProEtᵒᵖ)
        (b : (coefficientSequenceCommRingSheaf l L W).obj.obj (op (n, U.unop)))
        (a : (coefficientSequenceCommRingSheaf l E W).obj.obj (op (n, U.unop)))
        (x : (K.obj.X i).val.obj U),
        (δ.hom.f i).val.app (op (n, U.unop))
          (integralComparisonSequenceTensorSection l E L ι W ((d0.direct.obj K).X i)
            (op (n, U.unop)) b
            (integralComparisonSequenceSection.{u, u} l E W ((d0.direct.obj K).X i) n U
              ((((d0.directEvaluation n).inv.app K).f i).val.app U
                (integralScalarTensorSection.{u, u} l E E (AlgHom.id ℚ_[l] E) W n
                  (K.obj.X i) U a x)))) =
        integralComparisonSequenceSection.{u, u} l L W ((d.direct.obj K).X i) n U
          ((((d.directEvaluation n).inv.app K).f i).val.app U
            (integralScalarTensorSection.{u, u} l E L ι W n (K.obj.X i) U
              (((integralComparisonSequenceScalarMap.{u, u} l E L ι W).hom.app
                (op (n, U.unop))) a * b) x))
